strings.step.settings.sections.advanced.data.voi: Pass audio tags to the voice
strings.step.settings.sections.advanced.data_des: Spoken when the main agent cannot answer, for example because its AI provider is down, instead of ending the turn in silence. When empty: Sorry, I can't think right now. Please try again in a moment.

For satellites in avatar mode. Connect when woken: the satellite connects to LiveTalking when it wakes, about a second before the avatar shows. Always connected: the avatar is there at once, and each satellite keeps a LiveTalking session open. Recommended for the Chat show.

For satellites in avatar mode whose firmware has the switch "Avatar fed by Home Assistant". On: a reply goes to the satellite's avatar while it is still being made, so the avatar starts speaking sooner, and that switch is turned on. The satellite keeps the normal audio as a backup. Off: the satellite waits for the whole reply and sends it to the avatar itself, as before. Other satellites are not affected.

The tags this assistant's avatar is told about, separated by commas, such as happy, sad, excited. A reply that starts with one, such as [excited], tells LiveTalking that emotion. Any other tag of letters is still never spoken and counts as neutral. Each tag is one word of letters, at most 18. LiveTalking needs talking frames for a tag, or it shows neutral. When empty: neutral, happy, sad, angry, sarcastic.

Which face the avatar shows when a reply opens with an audio tag and no emotion tag. One line per face: the face, a colon, then the audio tags that give it, separated by commas, for example sarcastic: mischievous, smug. The whole tag is compared, in any case; the first line that has it wins. A face must be on the Emotion tags list, or its line is ignored. A tag found nowhere gives neutral. The reply is not changed: the audio tag still goes to the voice. When empty, the built-in table shown in the field is used.

Seconds after a turn whose reply asked a question. Within that time, the answer on the same satellite counts as the same person's, also without a voice match: a satellite listens for an answer without a wake word and often makes no match for it. A new voice match still decides. Every other turn needs a voice match of its own. 0: never, so an answer is refused unless the satellite matches it.

Seconds after the satellite starts listening. Until then, a turn whose helper still says pending waits for the voice match; after a longer request it has already arrived. A turn without a match of its own by then is refused with "Sorry, I can't tell who is speaking right now", unless it answers a question the assistant asked. A match counts as the turn's own when it was written after the satellite started listening for it. LANovo and EchoLocal displays match 4.6 to 5.5 seconds after the wake word.

Used for a request that neither a voice_speaker helper nor a Home Assistant user decides: a typed request when no user is chosen under Person 1 or Person 2, or a request from a device that has no helper and no user.
Added to the main agent's prompt after the persona. Explains the name labels in the shared history.

For a voice that understands audio tags, such as [laughs], [whispers] or [out of breath after running]: directions in square brackets, without digits. On: this assistant's voice is given the tags and they are never shown. Off: the tags are taken out, so no voice reads one aloud. A one-word tag at the very start that is on the Emotion tags list sets the avatar's face and is never passed to the voice. A short reply keeps its tags only when the assistant speaks through its avatar voice; announcements never do.

strings.step.settings.sections.agents.data_descr: Answers Person 1 and Person 2, with its normal tools.
strings.step.settings.sections.agents.name: Agents
strings.step.settings.sections.calendars.data.ca: Catch up after a restart for at most
strings.step.settings.sections.calendars.data_de: Used for a calendar that has no time of its own.
After a restart, events that became due while Home Assistant was off are still announced when they are less than this late. Later ones are dropped.
Called for every event that is due, with the variables owner, title, line, assistant, calendar, start, end, all_day and kind. When empty, only the voice_assistant_manager_calendar_due event is fired.
strings.step.settings.sections.calendars.descrip: For announcing events from calendars. Which calendars are watched is set under Configure > Calendars. These settings apply to all of them.
strings.step.settings.sections.calendars.name: Calendars
strings.step.settings.sections.chat.data_descrip: How this assistant behaves in a chat, for example: a dry, put-upon butler. A good start is to copy the personality part of the main agent's prompt, and leave out everything about controlling the home or using tools. At most 2000 characters. When empty, Extra instructions for announcements under Reminders is used.
The engine that speaks this assistant's chat lines. When empty, the voice of the speaker that hosts the chat is used.

A voice of that engine. On the Voice Manager page, an engine that lists its voices offers them to choose from. Otherwise type the voice as the engine expects it, which for many engines is the voice's id and not its name. When empty, the engine's default voice is used.
strings.step.settings.sections.chat.description: Used only when this assistant talks with another one in a chat show, never in normal conversations. A chat line is written by the announcement agent, which has no tools, so this assistant can only talk, never control the home.
strings.step.settings.sections.chat.name: Chat show
strings.step.settings.sections.favorites.data_de: Switches favorites on for this assistant: playing, saving and forgetting them by voice, and the lists on My assistant. While it is off, this assistant does not use favorites at all. A request that is exactly play and a favorite's name, such as play Radio 2 or play Radio 2 on the Denon, plays at once, without the main agent. Person 1's and Person 2's own favorites are shared by every assistant with this switched on.
strings.step.settings.sections.favorites.descrip: Named radio stations, podcasts and playlists that Person 1 and Person 2 can play by voice. Never used for an unknown voice.
strings.step.settings.sections.favorites.name: Favorites
strings.step.settings.sections.local.data.leave_: Leave questions and music searches to the main agent
strings.step.settings.sections.local.data_descri: A request that matches a built-in command exactly is carried out at once, without the main agent. Anything else goes to the main agent.
State questions such as is the door closed, and play music requests, go to the main agent even when a built-in command matches.
strings.step.settings.sections.local.description: Home Assistant's own quick commands, such as turn off the kitchen lights. They are only tried for Person 1 and Person 2, never for an unknown voice. For this to be the only way in, switch off Prefer handling commands locally on the Home Assistant voice assistants (pipelines) that use this assistant.
strings.step.settings.sections.local.name: Built-in commands
strings.step.settings.sections.memory.data.agent: Agent that decides what to save
strings.step.settings.sections.memory.data.auto_: Save important facts without being asked
strings.step.settings.sections.memory.data.enabl: Remember things about the people who live here
strings.step.settings.sections.memory.data.share: Share what each person tells it with the other person
strings.step.settings.sections.memory.data.use_g: Use the lists shared by all assistants
strings.step.settings.sections.memory.data_descr: Reads each exchange after the reply has been given, so it never slows an answer down. Pick a cheap, fast agent with no tool providers. It may not be the main agent or this assistant.
When off, only remember and forget requests change the memory.
Also the most facts shown to the main agent. When a list is full, the oldest facts saved without being asked are dropped first.

Like a person would, the assistant knows what either of you told it, whoever is speaking, so one of you can leave a message for the other. Facts a person asks to keep private are only used when that person speaks. When off, each person's facts are only used when that person speaks.
Facts are kept per assistant unless the person asks for all assistants to remember them.
strings.step.settings.sections.memory.descriptio: Lets this assistant remember what Person 1 and Person 2 tell it. It is never used for an unknown voice. View and edit the facts under Memory in the Configure menu.
strings.step.settings.sections.memory.name: Memory
strings.step.settings.sections.near_miss.data.en: Ask to try again on a near miss
strings.step.settings.sections.near_miss.data.mi: Lowest score that counts as a near miss
strings.step.settings.sections.near_miss.data.pe: Instructions for the try again reply
strings.step.settings.sections.near_miss.data_de: One line per row. Used when fixed lines are chosen above, or when the refusal agent fails or is slow.
Compared with the Last speaker score sensor of the satellite. Scores from this value up to the satellite's own recognition level get the try again reply.
strings.step.settings.sections.near_miss.descrip: For an unknown voice whose match score came close. The answer is still a refusal without tools, but it asks them to try again.
strings.step.settings.sections.near_miss.name: Almost recognised
strings.step.settings.sections.owner.data.name: Name
strings.step.settings.sections.owner.data_descri: Put in front of this person's messages in the shared history, for example Alex.
Instructions added to the main agent's prompt when this person speaks.

Every typed request made while logged in as this user counts as this person: from the phone app, the browser or the REST API, even one that names a satellite. Once any user is chosen, other logged-in users count as an unknown voice. Voice requests from a satellite go by its voice_speaker helper.
strings.step.settings.sections.owner.description: Used when the voice_speaker helper says owner, or when this person's Home Assistant user sends a typed request.
strings.step.settings.sections.owner.name: Person 1
strings.step.settings.sections.partner.data.name: Name
strings.step.settings.sections.partner.data_desc: Put in front of this person's messages in the shared history, for example Sam.
Instructions added to the main agent's prompt when this person speaks.

Every typed request made while logged in as this user counts as this person: from the phone app, the browser or the REST API, even one that names a satellite. Once any user is chosen, other logged-in users count as an unknown voice. Voice requests from a satellite go by its voice_speaker helper.
strings.step.settings.sections.partner.descripti: Used when the voice_speaker helper says partner, or when this person's Home Assistant user sends a typed request.
strings.step.settings.sections.partner.name: Person 2
strings.step.settings.sections.reminders.data.ca: The main agent can cancel reminders
strings.step.settings.sections.reminders.data.en: The main agent can set reminders
strings.step.settings.sections.reminders.data.fa: Line spoken when a reminder could not be set
strings.step.settings.sections.reminders.data_de: Writes every line this assistant announces: spoken reminders (the compose_announcement action) and calendar events. Must have no tool providers, and may not be the main agent or an assistant. When empty, the agent that writes the refusal is used.

The name this assistant goes by in reminders, for example jeeves. The main agent passes it to create_reminder, and compose_announcement uses it to find this assistant. When empty, the first word of the assistant's name is used.

Tells the main agent it may cancel a reminder, one-off or repeating, with the cancel_reminder tool, and replaces a reply that says a reminder is cancelled when the tool did not cancel one. Off: the main agent is told it cannot, and to point to the reminder calendar. To make sure it never can, also stop exposing script.cancel_reminder to Assist.
Adds reminder rules to the main agent's prompt, including who is speaking, and replaces a reply that says a reminder is set when the create_reminder tool did not set one.
When empty, a plain line is used.
My assistant lists these calendars' reminders for everyone. A calendar listed here cannot also be a personal one, but several assistants may list the same household calendar.
My assistant lists Person 1's reminders from these calendars. A calendar can belong to one Home Assistant user only, so Person 1 needs a Home Assistant user under People.
My assistant lists Person 2's reminders from these calendars. A calendar can belong to one Home Assistant user only, so Person 2 needs a Home Assistant user under People.

Used for spoken reminders and for calendar events alike, whoever they are for. The place for this assistant's character. Added after the recipient's persona and in front of the built-in announcement instructions. Not used for normal conversations.
strings.step.settings.sections.reminders.descrip: For a Home Assistant set up with a create_reminder script exposed to the main agent. Tells the main agent how to use it, keeps reminders out of memory, and writes spoken reminder lines in this assistant's style.
strings.step.settings.sections.reminders.name: Reminders
strings.step.settings.sections.strangers.data_de: One line per row. One is picked at random when fixed lines are chosen, or when the refusal agent fails or is slow.
What the refusal agent is told about the person speaking.
Must be an agent with no tool providers that exists. It may not be the main agent or another assistant of Voice Assistant Manager. It may not be able to control the home.
strings.step.settings.sections.strangers.descrip: An unknown voice never reaches the main agent or any tool, and the exchange is kept out of the shared history.
strings.step.settings.sections.strangers.name: Unknown voices
strings.step.settings.title: Voice persona settings
